name: Huetar
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Portilla, Mario. 2022 [online 2021]. Etimología huetar de la palabra toboba 'serpiente venenosa'. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 48(1): e48896. doi:10.15517/rfl.v48i1.48896 (Redalyc JATS PDF, open access)
catalog_locator: Sec. 4 'Derivación de la palabra toboba', p. 9 (last three paragraphs) to p. 10 (first two paragraphs); article unpaginated (e48896).
catalog_quote: Debido a que los materiales disponibles del huetar son escasos, las consideraciones respecto de los suprasegmentales en esta lengua son tentativas. Quesada Pacheco (1996, pp. 113-114) propone la posibilidad de que el huetar hubiera tenido acento. Hasta el momento no hay manera de saber con certeza si este habría sido predecible o no. Sin embargo, llama la atención que la mayor parte de las palabras del sustrato huetar en el español de Costa Rica lleva el acento en la última sílaba. Incluso, Quesada Pacheco (1996, p. 114) ha logrado determinar que, en el caso de vocablos sufijados, el presunto acento se ha corrido a la derecha de la raíz de la palabra hasta el lugar que ocupa un sufijo: Tayut > Tayutic ~ Tuyotique ~ Toyotique. De esta forma, el huetar parece compartir con otras lenguas de la rama ístmica la regla de corrimiento del acento a la posición final de la palabra. Un ejemplo significativo de la aplicación de dicha regla puede encontrarse en la palabra bocaracá 'variedad de serpiente (Bothriechis schlegelii)', la cual al ser comparada sus cognados en bribri y en cabécar ..., muestra un cambio del lugar original del acento, que pasa de la sílaba final de la raíz a la sílaba que contiene el formativo (de significado desconocido, en este caso): *bokará + ka > bocara-cá.

new_statements.translation: Because the available Huetar materials are scarce, considerations about suprasegmentals in this language are tentative. Quesada Pacheco (1996: 113-114) proposes the possibility that Huetar had stress. So far there is no way to know for certain whether it would have been predictable or not. However, it is striking that most of the Huetar substrate words in Costa Rican Spanish bear stress on the last syllable. [...] Thus Huetar seems to share with other languages of the Isthmic branch the rule shifting stress to word-final position.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tentative: Huetar probably had word stress, falling on the final syllable of the word; when suffixes/formatives are added stress shifts rightward onto them (Tayut > Tayutíc; *bokará + ka > bocaracá), i.e. an Isthmic-Chibchan-type stress-to-final rule. Evidence is indirect (Hispanicized substrate words and toponyms); the author states it cannot be established whether stress was predictable.
new_statements.exceptions: Only 'la mayor parte' (most) substrate words are final-stressed, implying some are not (e.g. súrtuba cited elsewhere in the article with non-final stress); no systematic exceptions discussed. Constenla 1984:7 warns that accent marks in the colonial sources are inconsistent and declines to infer anything.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, inferred from the stress of Huetar loanwords/toponyms as pronounced in Costa Rican Spanish and from colonial spellings; not from native-speaker data (language extinct since c. 1700). Portilla partly reports Quesada Pacheco 1996:113-114 second-hand; the final-stress generalization and the stress-shift rule are his own.
new_statements.identity_note: Huetar proper (huet1235), the extinct Chibchan language of Costa Rica's Central Valley; all statements rest on colonial-era name lists and on Huetar substrate vocabulary/toponyms surviving in Central Valley Spanish, not on speaker data. Descendant communities (Quitirrisí, Zapatón) speak only Spanish.

sources.note: Sec. 4 (pp. 9-10): tentative; cites Quesada Pacheco 1996:113-114 for the proposal that Huetar had stress; cannot be known whether it was predictable; but most Huetar substrate words in Costa Rican Spanish carry final stress, in suffixed words stress moves rightward onto the suffix (Tayut > Tayutic), so Huetar 'parece compartir con otras lenguas de la rama ístmica la regla de corrimiento del acento a la posición final de la palabra' (e.g. *bokará + ka > bocara-cá).
